Section 1 · pages 1-103 to 1-110

Navigation system

The navigation system consists of the gyro platform reference system, the navigation computer, the air data computer (ADC) and radio navigation equipment (Figure 1-60). The gyro platform reference system consists of a main and a standby platform, the radio navigation system of TACAN, ADF and marker beacon receiver. All systems are closely interfaced to supply complete navigational information throughout all flight phases.

NAV architecture (Figure 1-60): TACAN control panel and TACAN / RSBN switch feed the TACAN set, which with the navigation control panel feeds the adapter assembly; the adapter, the pitot static system (via the ADC, TAS indicator and altimeter) and the main / standby gyro system feed the navigation computer. Outputs go to the AFCS, ADI, HSI, HUD and fire control system; the ADF feeds the HSI.

The navigation system provides the aircraft position and the required steering commands for flying to a predetermined destination via up to three waypoints, either manually entered or from a TACAN station. It gives continuous readout of aircraft position in latitude and longitude, ground track, distance and time to the waypoints, and supplies the data for the HUD and HDD displays.

24
Section 1 · pages 1-104 to 1-110

Gyros and navigation computer

Gyro systems

Measure bank and pitch angles, course and acceleration along the axis of the platform; supply the primary azimuth and attitude reference and additionally supply direction, velocity and distance inputs to the navigation computer. The system uses DC power from the generator or the batteries; 115 VAC and 3 phases 36 VAC are supplied by the AC generator and the transformer, or by the PTO. However, PTO capacity is insufficient to supply heating power to the gyro system.

The unit consists of the main and the standby gyros, an analog / digital computer, operating controls for variation (behind the ejection seat) and latitude, a flux valve and BITE. Each system uses a gyro-stabilized platform on which three accelerometers are mounted; with the platform stabilized in pitch and roll by gyros and oriented along the aircraft axis, the accelerometers sense acceleration in any direction. This acceleration is processed by the analog / digital computer to provide course reference, attitude information, main gyro platform stabilization and signals for the navigation computer. A circuitry corrects for apparent precession, based on preset latitude.

Gyro alignment

With the BAT-GND SUPPLY switch and the generator and navigation switches placed to ON, power is applied to bring the gyro platforms to operating temperature. MAIN and STBY switches are selected for stabilization of the platforms; prior to alignment the appropriate aerodrome has to be selected.

Started by placing the MAIN and STBY gyro switches to ON, PREPARE / OPERATE switch in PREPARE. After approximately 30 to 40 sec, heading reference is inserted to the analog / digital computer by pressing the mag heading slave button and COURSE CMPTR ZERO pushbutton simultaneously for 10 to 15 sec. The PREPARE / OPERATE switch has to be placed to OPERATE within 90 sec after switching both gyros to ON. After a total time of 3 minutes, the fast prepare light on the right console rear panel illuminates, indicating completion of the alignment and system readiness; the light distinguishes during takeoff when the weight is off the main landing gear.

The PREPARE / OPERATE switch is left in the PREPARE position until the NAV READY light illuminates on the right console rear panel after 15 minutes, indicating completion of the alignment. Alignment may last up to 20 minutes at temperatures between −30 °C and −60 °C. When switching the PREPARE / OPERATE switch to OPERATE, the light extinguishes, indicating system readiness.

Note

If long alignment has been selected, and circumstances dictate switchover to fast alignment, at least 5 minutes should elapse prior to switching from PREPARE to OPERATE.

The gyro system can be operated with the main gyro platform or with the standby gyro platform; the main platform is more accurate since digital integration is provided to the main gyro platform only. In case of a main gyro system failure, switchover from main to standby has to be accomplished manually.

Indications: MASTER CAUTION light flashing · AEKRAN MAIN DIR VERT GYRO / STBY DIR VERT GYRO / TWO DIR VERT GYRO — failure of the corresponding gyro system(s) · ADI gyro fail light.

Navigation computer

The central unit of the navigation system. It processes data from the inertial navigation unit and the air data computer (ADC) to compute the present position and to correct it according to TACAN signals, to compute azimuth and distance information to a selected, programmed navigation point, and altitude deviations as well as ground track information. Additionally it produces discrete control signals for automatic control of the complete navigation system. Powered by 28.5 VDC, 115 VAC and 3 phases 36 VAC.

To reduce required computational capacity, a relative coordinate system restricted in latitude and longitude is used; the zero point is in the lower left corner. Required navigation points are entered via the navigation computer programming panel, located on the lower left side of the nose section. Two types are available, CWU A-340-071M version 2204 and version 2205. Version 2204 is restricted in latitude and longitude to an area of 36° and one set of coordinates; version 2205 to an area of 40° and two sets of coordinates.

Operating modes

ModeCharacteristics
DEAD RECKONINGAvailable after fast alignment, only analog integration of both gyro platforms. Accuracy: 4 % of distance travelled per hour of circular error probability, 1.5° precession per hour. Since no aerological wind data are processed, large computational errors may be present
INERTIAL NAVIGATIONAvailable after long alignment with the main gyro platform. Since precise alignment was performed, maximum error is 4.5 NM per hour of circular error probability, precession 1° per hour
UPDATEAutomatic continuous computer update available in both operating modes. System inaccuracy reduced to ±0.2 NM +0.1 % of distance to the station used for update. Three individual TACAN stations can be programmed prior to flight
VISUAL UPDATEManual update by pressing the COURSE CMPTR ZERO illuminated pushbutton and releasing it upon overflight of a selected and programmed waypoint or airfield

Swipe the table sideways →

Note

Update is not possible if a discrepancy of more than 21 NM exists between the present position computed and the actual position.

For TACAN update: the channel select switch must be placed to AUTO, the REL BEARING switch to RSBN, and the landing switch to OFF; TACAN is selected on the RH console. The CORR light illuminates if proper signals are received and automatic update is performed. For update with a TACAN station, the programmed station must be selected on the TACAN control panel additionally.

Navigational options

Operated according to the setting on the navigation control panel: point-to-point navigation · return · landing approach · traffic re-entry (missed approach) · manual station select.

  • Point-to-point: six navigation points can be programmed, selected with the WP-A/D switch and one of the three WP-A/D illuminated pushbuttons. Course is displayed by the course pointer and course window, distance by the range indicator on the HSI and HUD. As the aircraft closes on the selected coordinate, the D < 21 NM light illuminates. Passing the coordinate, the last bearing indication will be shown until exceeding 3.2 NM distance outbound.
  • Return: provides bearing information to a lead point for the nearest 9.2 NM final intercept to the selected airfield, provided the correct landing direction is selected with the COURSE switch and the update function is operating. Slant range is indicated to the selected A/D coordinates. If automatic update is inoperative, course and distance to the aerodrome reference point are provided. During the approach, glide path information is displayed on the ADI for a 7° glide slope to the final intercept point at 3 700 ft AGL or QFE.
  • Traffic re-entry (missed approach): pressing the missed approach button provides steering for a traffic pattern, provided the landing select switch is off and TACAN correction is operative. Steering is provided for a 5.4 NM downwind leg and final intercept; pattern direction left or right hand is selected with the circle left-right switch. Glidepath information is displayed for a pattern altitude of 2 000 ft AGL or QFE.
  • Manual station select: with the channels MAN / AUTO switch in MAN, bearing and distance to a selected TACAN station is displayed; navigation computer update is not provided.
Note

With the CHANNELS switch in manual, the final course must be dialed in on the HSI to receive steering commands.

Navigation computer programming

Programming panel on the lower left side of the nose section (Figure 1-62A) programs: reference latitude for the coordinate square · relative coordinates for 3 airfields, 3 waypoints, 3 beacons · RWY direction for 3 airfields between 0° to 179.9° · heading for 4 visual heading reference points (not in use) · reference heading for parking spot (not in use) · 3 RSBN channels · 3 ILS channels. A second set of data has to be programmed with computer CWU version 2205, restricted to a 40° area, but it cannot be selected from the cockpit.

Reference latitude: in the Northern hemisphere, the lateral geographical coordinate complemented by three zeros; in the Southern hemisphere, the lateral geographical coordinates subtracted from 360 and the result complemented by two zeros.

Coordinates: the relative coordinate is calculated to an accuracy of four decimals, rounded to the third decimal and expressed as an unfragmented number. Relative coordinates are obtained by subtracting the reference coordinates of the relative coordinate system from the geographical coordinates.

arc degrees + arc min / 60 + arc sec / 3600 = five-digit code

Sample from the manual: geographical 54°20′22″N, 07°34′56″E with reference 30°00′00″N, 10°00′00″W gives relative 24°20′22″ and 17°34′56″. Latitude 24 + 0.3333 + 0.0061 = 24.3394 → code 24339; longitude 17 + 0.5666 + 0.0155 = 17.5822 → code 17582. Combined with address number 41 and prefix 0 for waypoint 3 relative latitude, the programming code is 41024339.

Entering the data set: DC and AC power must be available and the NAVIGATION switch on the system power panel switched ON. Switch the panel on with the ВКЛ ОТКЛ (ON) button; illumination of the data input display indicates system readiness. Press the СБРОС (RESET) pushbutton to set the display to zero. Before entering the data set in random sequence, the opening code 77127777 has to be entered. After each eight-digit code press ЗАП (ENTER). After input of the complete data set, the closing code 77139999 has to be entered. With CWU version 2205, code 25100001 follows the opening code for the first data set, and 25100002 for the second. The ЧТЕН (READOUT) button checks valid codes.

RSBN / ILS channels: entered in coded format for navigation computer update. Since RSBN and ILS are presently not in use, the appropriate code list is not published in GAF T.O. 1F-MIG29-1; however, a random code still has to be entered to permit NAV computer update by use of TACAN stations.

Indication: AEKRAN NAVIG COMPUTER — no NAV system update.

Section 1 · pages 1-111 to 1-115

Radio navigation: TACAN, ADF, IFF

TACAN

Provides magnetic bearing and slant range to the selected ground station, or to a suitably equipped cooperating aircraft (air-to-air). The system can transmit only distance information when interrogated in the A/A, T/R mode, determines the identity of the transmitting station and indicates the dependability of the transmitted signal.

It uses radio navigation frequencies whose propagation is virtually limited to line of sight. In case of co-channel interference in T/R mode, the interfering channel identifier is garbled. When a temporary loss of signals occurs, a memory keeps range tracking for 15 seconds and bearing tracking for 3 seconds. The TACAN automatically self-tests after a temporary signal loss and displays its status on the control panel; supplied with 115 VAC by the AC generator or the PTO. An upper and a lower antenna receive TACAN signals; switching to the antenna with the greatest signal strength is automatic.

TACAN function selector (Figure 1-63)

PositionFunction
OFFPower disconnected
RECReceive mode, no interrogation pulse transmitted. Bearing identification of a selected ground station is received; range information is not available
T/RTransmit / receive mode: transmitter and receiver active, generating range and bearing information from a selected ground station
A/A RECAir-to-air receive: receives and decodes bearing information from a suitably equipped cooperating aircraft. The channel of the receiving aircraft must be either 63 channels above or 63 channels below the cooperating aircraft's channel, within the 1 through 126 X or Y channel range; both must be on the same X or Y channel
A/A T/RAir-to-air transmit / receive: interrogates a reference aircraft and displays slant range to the cooperating aircraft. Provides distance replies to other aircraft when interrogated; bearing to a suitably equipped cooperating aircraft is also displayed. The TACAN AN/ARN-118 can transmit only distance information in A/A T/R mode; the maximum number of aircraft receiving range information simultaneously is 5

Swipe the table sideways →

Note
  • In the air-to-air modes, to prevent possible interference from IFF or transponder signals, channels 1 thru 11, 58 thru 74 and 121 thru 126 should not be used.
  • To reduce the possibility of DME interference, the use of Y channels is recommended if the suitably equipped cooperating aircraft is Y channel capable.

Channel selector control: two rotary knobs set the desired channel — the left knob selects the tens and hundreds digits, the right knob the units digits and contains an outer knob which selects the X or Y channel. Placing the knob to X provides 126 channel operation; Y adds an additional 126 channel capability. The dial system is numbered 0 to 129, each number from 1 to 126 representing a specific pair of transmitting and receiving frequencies; numbers 0, 127, 128 and 129 are not usable. The selected channel is displayed in the NAV channel window followed by X or Y.

TACAN test: TACAN / RSBN switch to TACAN · REL BEARING switch to RSBN · function selector T/R · allow 90 sec for warm-up · press and release the test button. Observe: test indicator light flashes momentarily · HSI distance indicates 0.0 ±0.5 miles (−0.5 miles indicated as 399.5 miles) · bearing pointer slew to 180° ±3° · after about 15 sec, normal TACAN lock-on. This test does not check the antenna interface; accuracy should be checked against a ground check point.

Automatic self-test: if the TACAN bearing signal becomes lost or unreliable, the system switches to automatic self-test. If the test indicator light illuminates steady during the test cycle in both T/R and REC modes, the bearing and distance information on the HSI is invalid. The self-test can be terminated by turning either the function selector knob or any of the channel selector knobs.

Inflight confidence test: set the function selector to T/R and press the TACAN test button; the test indicator light flashes momentarily. If the light illuminates steady during the test cycle in both T/R and REC modes, bearing and distance information are invalid. If the light comes on in the T/R mode but not in the REC mode, the distance information is invalid and the bearing on the HSI is valid.

Adapter assembly TACAN / RSBN

Converts TACAN signals to match NAV system requirements. Since RSBN inputs to the NAV system refer to true north, TACAN signals must be corrected for variation to simulate RSBN signals; DC power is required. Adaptation is limited to three programmed TACAN stations selected with the BEACON buttons, CHANNEL select switch in AUTO. Requirements: TACAN / RSBN switch TACAN · CHANNEL select AUTO · BEACON 1, 2 or 3 selected · TACAN control panel channel selected corresponding to the beacon.

TACAN / RSBN switch (RH console): two-position toggle switch selecting the appropriate system as reference for the navigation system; the RSBN light illuminates when RSBN is selected.

Automatic direction finding

The ADF provides direction finding or radio monitoring in the HF frequency band (150 to 1 299.5 kHz). Eight different stations can be channelized for inflight use; however, a standard setting is normally programmed. Powered by 28.5 VDC and 36 VAC from a transformer; battery and DC/AC converter supply the system in case of a generator failure.

Controls: ADF select switch on the radio panel · REL BEARING / ADF switch on the navigation panel · INNER / OUTER switch and BEACON INNER light on the instrument panel above the radar altimeter · ADF channel select knob · VOICE / CW switch · COMPASS / ANTENNA select switch · VOL control knob · LOOP pushbutton (Figure 1-65). GT: the INNER / OUTER switch and BEACON INNER light are on the LH side wall.

ADF operation: ADF select switch (radio panel) to off · RSBN / ADF select switch (navigation panel) to ADF · COMPASS / ANTENNA switch to COMP · INNER / OUTER switch to the desired position (check the BEACON inner light is illuminated if INNER is selected) · select the desired channel with the ADF channel select knob · VOICE / CW switch as required.

ADF radio receiver operation: ADF select switch to ADF · RSBN / ADF to ADF · COMPASS / ANTENNA to ANTENNA · select the desired channel · VOICE / CW as required.

Self-test: RSBN / ADF switch to ADF · ADF channel select knob to position P — check bearing pointer rotating to approximately 195° · VOICE / CW switch to CW — check for 800 Hz tone transmission. The LOOP pushbutton manually rotates the ADF loop antenna; the antenna returns to its original position upon release.

Radio marker receiver

Indicates the overflight of a marker beacon; frequency 75 MHz in accordance with ICAO standards. Overflight is indicated by illumination of the MARKER BEACON light on the TLP and an audio signal of 3 000 Hz. Operated by 28.5 VDC from the DC generator or battery power; switched on by placing the ACFT SYS switch to ON.

Note

The marker beacon receiver will switch the ADF from a selected OUTER channel to INNER channel when passing a marker beacon within 15° of the final course, provided the gear is down.

IFF equipment

The identification system STR 700 provides automatic identification of the aircraft when challenged by surface or airborne IFF interrogation sets; it identifies position momentarily upon request, reports the altitude of the aircraft and indicates an emergency. Altitude is given from the air data computer. Five modes of operation are provided:

Mode 1Security identification
Mode 2Personal identification
Mode 3/ATraffic identification
Mode CAltitude reporting
Mode 4Crypto identification

The codes for mode 1 (00-73) and 3/A can be set in the cockpit during flight, but the code for mode 2 must be set on the ground. Mode 2 and mode 3/A can be set from code 0 000 to 7 777. When mode C is selected, coded altitude information from the altitude encoder is applied to the IFF system for reply to mode C interrogation. There are no provisions to manually set mode C code. Failure of mode 4 reply is indicated by an optical and an audio signal. Supplied with 28.5 VDC and 115 VAC, 400 Hz for the altitude encoder.

IFF control panel on the right console (GT: front cockpit only). Master function selector — five-position rotary knob marked MASTER:

PositionFunction
OFFPower disconnected
STBYFull power supplied to the system, but with interrogation replies blocked
LOWSystem operates with reduced sensitivity; transmitted power from the transponder is the same for both LOW and NORM
NORMSystem operates at full sensitivity
EMERResponds in modes 1, 2, 3/A and C. The reply for modes 1 and 2 is a special emergency signal of the codes selected on the applicable dials, while mode 3/A replies a special emergency signal of code 7 700, regardless of the selected code

Swipe the table sideways →

Mode selector switches: four three-position toggle switches for modes 1, 2, 3/A and C — M1-MC enables the respective mode, OUT disables it, TEST is the springloaded self-test position in which the green TEST light illuminates when the respective mode is operating.

Position identification switch: three-position toggle switch used by the AC to provide momentary identification of position upon request — I/P enables identification of position replies in modes 1, 2, 3/A and C, continued for a 30 ±10 sec duration after the switch has been released; OUT disables identification of position capability; MIC is the same as I/P except the microphone button must be pressed.

Mode 1 code selector: rotary knob with two concentric wheels, 32 available 2-digit codes. Mode 2 code selectors: four code selectors, each settable from 0 to 7; the knob is removed upon completion of the setting on the ground. Mode 3/A code selector: two identical rotary knobs with two concentric wheels, 4 096 available 4-digit codes. Mode 4 selector switch: ON enables replies to mode 4 interrogations, OUT disables them.

Mode 4 function knob: four-position rotary knob marked MODE 4 — A answers interrogations using code A; B answers interrogations using code B; ZERO erases mode 4 code settings, provided the MASTER knob is not in OFF (both mode 4 codes are automatically erased after landing when the IFF system is switched off, except if the switch is placed to HOLD); HOLD retains mode 4 code settings if another flight is anticipated during the coded period — HOLD must be selected at least 15 seconds before system shut-down.

Mode 4 monitor switch: AUDIO / OUT / LIGHT — AUDIO indicates interrogation and reply of mode 4 by an audio signal and the lights REPLY and IFF; OUT disables all mode 4 audio / light indications; LIGHT disables audio and indicates mode 4 interrogation by the lights REPLY and IFF only. The green mode 4 reply indicator illuminates when mode 4 replies are transmitted, provided the monitor switch is in AUDIO or LIGHT. A green MODE 4 caption on the TLP illuminates if the aircraft is interrogated by a valid mode 4 signal but does not reply.

BIT check before each flight: test light (press-to-test) CHECK · master knob STBY (allow 2 minutes warm-up) · master knob NORM · mode 1 selector switch TEST and hold — the test light should illuminate; if not, the selected mode is at fault. Test modes 1, 3/A and C respectively. Before takeoff: master knob NORM, BIT check completed, perform the test according to the requests of the interrogating ground station.

Section 1 · pages 1-118 to 1-119

Armament, DASS, warning equipment

Armament system

Consists of the fire control system, the radar system, IRSTS / LRF and the associated weapons; described in GAF T.O. 1F-MIG29-34-1.

Defensive aids subsystem (DASS): RHAW system and flare dispenser, also described in GAF T.O. 1F-MIG29-34-1.

External stores: a variety of stores can be carried on the seven external stations. For stores configurations and limitations refer to section 5 of this manual; for loading and operation of armament and ECM equipment refer to the applicable weapons delivery manual.

Warning and information equipment

To keep instrument cross-check to a minimum, warning and indicator lights are incorporated throughout the cockpit; additional voice warning is provided for abnormal conditions. The equipment consists of three independent systems — TLP, AEKRAN and VIWAS. A MASTER CAUTION light flashes whenever a warning light illuminates on the TLP (red lights) or an AEKRAN warning signal is displayed.

Note

All warning equipment is operated with 28.5 VDC from the generator or battery power.

MASTER CAUTION light: located on the instrument panel. Whenever a warning signal is displayed on the TLP or the AEKRAN, it starts flashing. Brightness can be adjusted by rotating the light case; pressing the light extinguishes the lights, warnings on the TLP turn steady, AEKRAN displays are not affected.

Telelight panel: provides immediate warning of an abnormal condition which could affect the safety of the aircraft (red lights); additional information lights (green) indicate system operation or condition. A malfunction is indicated by a flashing warning light in conjunction with the flashing MASTER CAUTION light; after reset of the MASTER CAUTION light, the warning light illuminates steady until the problem is solved.

After modification with wing drop tanks: three previous spare captions have been modified to read WDT NO PRESS, WDT TEST and FEEL UNIT OK. WDT NO PRESS illuminates prior to engine start when wing drop tanks are installed, or during a wing drop tank pressurization failure; after engine start the caption extinguishes, indicating wing drop tank pressurization. Illumination of WDT TEST indicates a valid system check when the TEST WDT button on the control and test panel is pressed. FEEL UNIT OK replaces the identical caption removed from the control and test panel.

Warning light controls: a photodiode automatically adjusts brightness according to environmental conditions; a rheostat on the lighting panel provides manual adjustment.

TLP layouts (Figure 1-67)

Three variants are shown — G, GT front cockpit and GT rear cockpit. Captions across the G panel include: GBX FIRE · LH ENG FIRE / RH ENG FIRE · REDUCED RPM LH ENG / RH ENG · OIL PRESS LEFT / RIGHT · OIL GBX · 550 KG REMAIN · COC · DOUBLE HYD SYS · DAMPER OFF · LH ENG AB / RH ENG AB · LH ENG START / RH ENG START · RUD TRIM NEUTRAL · STAB TRIM NEUTRAL · AIL TRIM NEUTRAL · FEEL UNIT TO / LD · MARKER BEACON · EMERG HYD PUMP ON · MODE 4 · NAV READY. The GT panels add DOUBLE HYD SYS, ATT, AUTO RECOVER, APPROACH, MISSED APPROACH, SET COURSE INDICATOR, ALT HOLD.

AEKRAN indicator: lower center of the instrument panel, with FAL / TURN / ENGAGE buttons and a rotary SELECT knob. Voice warning buttons: REPEAT VOICE WARN and CHECK VOICE WARN, with the FAIL / IFF / ANTI COLL switch block.

Weapon and armament controls (Figure 1-67A)

Front side: flare control panel (OUTER / INNER, EMERG JETTISON, GROUND / FIRE) · ART S REMAINING counter set to 60 · HUD with BRIGHT, HUD selector (DAY / RETICLE) and TEST button · HDD with BRIGHT control · emergency missile jettison button (EMERG MSL JETT) · TAXI / OFF / LAND light switch · radar control panel (range scales 2, 4, 8, 16 / 1, 3, 10, 20, 50, ΔH, HEAD ON, CLOSE COMBAT, AUTO, RILLUM / OFF, PURSUIT, COMP / TWF, AO / RILLUM, IR, RBS) · IR VOLUME and RUDDER TRIM (LEFT / RIGHT) · RHAW display panel (SOUND OFF, TEST, BRIGHT, RING) · flare dispenser DISPENSE READY / DISPENSE CHECK · weapon control panel (MASTER ARM-ARM with SAVE, ZONE A/B, A/G, PREPARE MAN, RADAR / IR / HELM selector, WCS MODES OPT / BI, IR GAIN HL / BRIGHT, 0.5 ALL, MED SPANT / LARGE, SIN / RBS, ALL) · control stick.

Section 1 · pages 1-120 to 1-122

AEKRAN and VIWAS

AEKRAN

Part of the aircraft warning and recording system. It monitors and controls the operation of aircraft systems and self-test equipment, and displays and records corresponding messages if malfunctions occur. After landing, additional information about aircraft systems, equipment and exceeding of limitations not relevant for the safety of flight, and illumination of red warning lights, are recorded by discrete signals.

Activated automatically when the NAVIGATION switch is placed to on; during engine start, both generators failure indication may be displayed until external power is disconnected. After takeoff, FLIGHT illuminates momentarily. If a malfunction is detected, the corresponding message is displayed, the MASTER CAUTION light flashes and VIWAS gives the appropriate message; if no appropriate message is available, VIWAS signals Check AEKRAN.

The indication is displayed until the problem indicated is solved, a signal with higher priority is received or the AEKRAN CALL button is pressed. Pressing AEKRAN CALL extinguishes the indication and the MASTER CAUTION light, however the signal is stored in the memory circuit indicated by a memory light. If two or more systems fail, the turn light illuminates and the highest priority signal is displayed first; depressing AEKRAN CALL stores the displayed signal in the memory circuit and permits display of the next signal in the priority sequence line. After all signals have been displayed, the turn light extinguishes. After landing, all stored signals are copied to a control slip; after engine shut-down, AC GEN is displayed on the AEKRAN.

Self-test: push the AEKRAN CALL button; the fail light must not illuminate. After 15 seconds, SELF TEST followed by OK are displayed. AEKRAN CALL button: triple use — initiates self-test, calls up signals in the priority sequence line, recalls signals in the memory circuit. FAIL light indicates a system failure; TURN light indicates that signals of lower priority are held in the priority sequence line; MEMORY light indicates signals in the memory circuit.

Voice information and warning system

Provides voice warning to focus the pilot's attention to a problem indicated on the warning light panel or AEKRAN; depending on the type of emergency, advisory for initial action to be taken is added. Powered by 28.5 VDC. In case of multiple malfunctions, voice warnings are realised according to the priority list; warnings No. 1, 2, 3 and 5 are simultaneously transmitted over the radio.

Switched on with the battery; two pushbuttons on the RH console (Figure 1-70): CHECK VOICE WARN initiates a self-test, REPEAT VOICE WARN repeats the last warning. The same panel carries the AM / FM switch and the ANTI COLL switch.

Warning light test: to ensure utmost reliability, the light bulbs of all warning and indicator lights are function tested — pressing the LAMP TEST button on the lighting panel illuminates all lights.

Weapon and armament controls — LH / RH side (Figure 1-67B)

Coverage note

What this scan contains

Gap in the source

The list of effective pages in this scan announces all seven sections plus the appendices — Section 2 Normal Procedures (2-1 to 2-8), Section 3 Emergency Procedures (3-1 to 3-16), Section 4 Crew Duties (4-1 to 4-2), Section 5 Operating Limitations (5-1 to 5-17), Section 6 Flight Characteristics (6-1 to 6-23), Section 7 All Weather Operation (7-1 to 7-3), Appendix A Performance Data, Appendix B Cockpit Marking Reference and the Index. None of those pages are in this file: the PDF runs 157 pages and ends with the Section 1 servicing diagram at page 1-124. This page therefore carries the front matter and Section 1 complete, and nothing from sections 2–7.

The manual's own note on the MiG-29 GT trainer applies throughout: the trainer has no radar and no gun-firing radar mode, though it can still employ IR missiles and the gun; its rear cockpit carries a radar simulation control panel and a periscope for ground operation.
